newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake Energy responds to lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake Energy responds to lawsuit.

text.p: Chesapeake Energy Corp said that Union Pacific Resources Group's lawsuit alleging violation of a patent for horizontal drilling technology is not valid and therefore was not violated.
Chesapeake, based in Oklahoma City, saw it hadn't yet reviewed thoroughly the complaint, but its advice from patent counsel was that it was not valid.

"Chesapeake intends to vigorously defend the lawsuit which it believes to be an abuse of process designed solely to seek a strategic advantage in the geographic areas in which the companies operate," Chesapeake said in a statement.
The company has had drilling success using the technology, recently in the promising Louisiana Chalk Trend area where two wells showed promising results.

Chesapeake's shares have risen sharply in the last 12 months, going from a low of just over $12 to a high above $70. They stood at $62-3/4 mid-morning Thursday. The company also has been the subject of a controversial short squeeze, whereby some investors sold stock in the company which they didn't own in expectation its price would fall.
Union Pacific Resources Group said Wednesday that it has filed a lawsuit against Chesapeake Energy Corp accusing it of infringing on a geosteering patent.
